data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The published distinction is that idempotency constrains the operation's effect on state, while safety constrains the operation's effect on correctness under retries. An append-only event log requires safety: writers must ensure that duplicate appends\u2014inevitable under at-least-once delivery\u2014do not corrupt deterministic replay. This is achievable via content-addressable or sequence-numbered appends that make duplicates detectable, even though the raw append remains non-idempotent.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the reasoning system's replay engine does not perform deduplication, safety is not achieved and the log would require true idempotent appends\u2014which are impossible for an append-only structure without external state.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If published definitions define safety as identical to idempotency in the messaging context, the claimed distinction is illusory.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log allows arbitrary content without deterministic keys, duplicate detection is impossible and safety fails.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under at-least-once delivery, a writer may append the same event multiple times because the acknowledgment was lost. Idempotency would require that the second append have no additional effect\u2014impossible for a true append-only log. Safety only requires that the replayed log produce the same reasoning state, which holds if duplicate entries are filtered during replay by their deterministic keys. The log is safe under retries because the replay semantics absorb duplicates; it is not idempotent because the log's physical contents differ.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
